display_title: Fix jax.scipy.special.poch for large z where gamma overflows

head_commit.message:
Fix jax.scipy.special.poch for large z where gamma overflows

poch(z, m) was computed as gamma(z + m) / gamma(z), which returns nan or
inf once either gamma value overflows (z > ~35 in float32, z > ~171 in
float64). Fall back to gammaln(|m|) - betaln(min(z, z + m), |m|) in log
space in that case.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Fix gennorm.cdf losing precision in the lower tail

head_commit.message:
Fix gennorm.cdf losing precision in the lower tail

gennorm.cdf computed 0.5 * (1 + sign(x) * igamma(1/beta, |x|**beta)),
which for x < 0 is 0.5 * (1 - igamma(...)) and cancels once igamma
approaches 1, returning 0.0 for small lower-tail probabilities.
Compute the x < 0 branch directly as 0.5 * igammac(1/beta, |x|**beta).

Fixes #42765

display_title: Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

head_commit.message:
Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

Nsight Systems (`nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu --profile-from-start off`) only record what runs between `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop`. JAX users currently call these through custom `ctypes` wrappers.

`jax.profiler.start_capture()`, `jax.profiler.stop_capture()`, and the `jax.profiler.capture()` context manager call new `_profiler.start_capture` and `_profiler.stop_capture` bindings. The bindings load `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop` from `libcuda.so.1` at first use and raise an error if the driver is missing or the call fails. The calling thread needs a current CUDA context, which it has once it ran a JAX computation. The JAX functions raise `RuntimeError` on non-CUDA backends and on older jaxlib builds without the bindings.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

head_commit.message:
Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

`cache_key.get` currently strips `device_assignment` from serialized `CompileOptions` only on GPU. In multi-process CPU jobs, process-local `jit` calls carry each worker's global device ID in `device_assignment` (`[[0]]` on process 0 vs. `[[2048]]` on process 1). Since XLA:CPU compilation does not depend on `device_assignment`, non-zero processes miss persistent cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's strip `device_assignment` when hashing `CompileOptions` on CPU as well, matching GPU.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Use an atomic transaction in `tensorstore_impl.combine_kvstores`

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Use an atomic transaction in `tensorstore_impl.combine_kvstores`

`combine_kvstores` created a default non-atomic (`isolated`) `ts.Transaction()`
for OCDBT `experimental_copy_range_to`. TensorStore's OCDBT driver now guards
its transactional `ExperimentalCopyRangeFrom` fast path on atomic non-distributed
transactions (matching `ReadModifyWrite`, `TransactionalDeleteRange`, and
`TransactionalListImpl`), so non-atomic transactions return `UNIMPLEMENTED`
(`NotImplementedError: CopyRange not supported`).

Use `ts.Transaction(atomic=True)` in `combine_kvstores` (consistent with
`serialization_test.py` and Orbax's OCDBT merge path), and add a single-process
`CheckpointTest.test_combine_kvstores` unit test so `combine_kvstores` is covered
outside multiprocess tests.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

head_commit.message:
Donate PjRt-IFRT executable inputs according to donation intent.

`LoadedExecutable::GetDonatableInputIndices()` reports parameter donation intent (`jax.buffer_donor` and `tf.aliasing_output`), whereas XLA compilation may leave a donor unaliased when no compatible output buffer exists. Because post-compilation buffer aliasing is unpredictable to callers, `PjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute()` marks all inputs in `donatable_input_indices` (unless in `ExecuteOptions::non_donatable_input_indices`) as deleted after dispatch.

Bump `JAX_XLA_VERSION_NUMBER` to 91 and update JAX buffer donation tests to expect donated inputs to be deleted without aliasing.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Mark `LaxTest.testMulhiForwardCompatLowering` as thread-unsafe

`LaxTest.testMulhiForwardCompatLowering` patches module-global
`lax_internal.xla_version` to `78`, which races with concurrent tests under
multi-threaded execution (`JAX_TEST_NUM_THREADS > 0`). In particular,
`_log2_lower` checks `xla_version < 80`, causing concurrent `lax.log2` calls
in `LaxTest.testOp` to mix native `hlo.log2` and `hlo.log * (1 / ln(2))`
lowerings between eager and jitted execution.

Decorate `testMulhiForwardCompatLowering` with `@jtu.thread_unsafe_test()`
below `@jtu.sample_product(...)` so all parameterized variants run
sequentially on the main thread after thread-safe tests complete.

display_title: [pallas] Trace kernels with jit enabled under disable_jit

head_commit.message:
[pallas] Trace kernels with jit enabled under disable_jit

`pallas_call` and `mpmd_map` only cleared `disable_jit` at execution time, leaving it active during kernel tracing and breaking loops over `Ref` carries.

Fixes #42435
